Since the issue raised in the these appeals are similar, they are being decided by a common judgment.
The facts of First Appeal No.4424 of 2025 are taken for the purpose of adjudication.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4424/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined 2
Admit.
Learned AGPs Mr.Patel and Ms. Shah waive service of notice of admission.

3 The present appeal is filed under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, read with Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, challenging the judgment and award dated 13.05.2022 passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Bayad in Land Acquisition Reference Case No.197 of 2017,
whereby the learned Reference Court has awarded additional compensation at the rate of Rs.223/-
per square meter for the land acquired pertaining to village Dakhneshwar, pursuant to the notification issued under Section 4 of the Act dated 09.06.2005.
4

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Heard the learned advocate Mr. Aditya Patel for the claimant and the learned AGP Mr. Parth Patel for the defendant State.
5 It is submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Patel that the learned Reference Court has committed an error in awarding total compensation at the rate of Rs.223/- per square meter.

It is submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Patel that for the same Taluka, another acquisition was undertaken for village Madhav Kampo, wherein the notification under Section 4 of the Act was also issued on 09.06.2005 and the land was acquired for an irrigation scheme.

In the said case, the learned Reference Court NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4424/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.317/- per square meter, which judgment has been accepted by the State and the compensation as awarded has already been paid to the claimants.
5.1 It is further submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Patel that village Dakhneshwar shares a common boundary with Taluka Bayad, which is a municipal area having various civic amenities.

Therefore, even though village Madhav Kampo abuts the State Highway, considering the proximity and common boundary with Taluka Bayad, the compensation awarded to the present claimants deserves to be enhanced to Rs.317/- per square meter, as awarded in the case of village Madhav Kampo.
5.2 In the aforesaid background, learned advocate Mr. Patel has prayed for modification of the impugned judgment to the above extent 6

Per contra, learned AGP Mr. Parth Patel submits that the reliance placed by learned advocate Mr. Patel on the case of village Madhav Kampo is misconceived,
inasmuch as the land of village Madhav Kampo abuts the State Highway, and therefore, there is a natural escalation in the market value of the land.

It is submitted by the learned AGP Mr. Patel that village Dakhneshwar is situated at a distance of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4424/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined approximately 1.94 kilometers from village Madhav Kampo and several other villages intervene between the two.
It is therefore submitted by the learned AGP Mr. Patel that the lands are not comparable and no parity can be drawn between the two acquisitions.

In view of the aforesaid facts, the impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Patelvasantkumar Revabhai vs State Of Gujarat on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178605532/

sentences.text: Reference Court does not call for any interference, and the appeal deserves to be dismissed.

7 Having considered the submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties and upon perusal of the map as well as the reasons assigned by the learned Reference Court, it emerges that the land under acquisition pertaining to village Dakhneshwar, Taluka Bayad, District Aravalli,
was acquired for the purpose of an irrigation scheme by issuance of notifications under Sections 4, 5 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act on 14.10.2005.

The learned Special Land Acquisition Officer thereafter passed an award under Section 11 of the Act on 02.12.2005, determining the market value of the acquired land at the rate of Rs.6.40 per square meter, which came to be challenged by the claimant by filing a Reference under Section 18 of the Act seeking enhancement of compensation.

7.1 It further emerges that the learned Reference NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4424/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined Court, while adjudicating the Reference, relied upon the award pertaining to village Gopalpura in LAR No.122 of 2017 and determined the market value at the rate of Rs.216.60 per square meter.

However, on referring to the map, it is evident that village Gopalpura is situated near village Dhanrura and the distance between village Gopalpura and village Dakhneshwar is approximately 8.1 kilometers.
Undisputedly, such distant village cannot form a proper basis for determining the market value of the land under acquisition in the present case.
7.2 Therefore, the question that arises for consideration before this Court is as to what should be the appropriate basis for determining the market value of the land situated at village Dakhneshwar.
Learned advocate Mr. Patel has relied upon the award passed in respect of village Madhav Kampo.
On referring to the same, it emerges that village Dakhneshwar and village Madhav Kampo are situated on the same alignment.

It further emerges that village Madhav Kampo has a District Road touching the State Highway, whereas village Dakhneshwar shares common boundaries with Taluka Bayad, which also touches the State Highway.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4424/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined 7.3

On referring to the award passed by the learned Reference Court in respect of village Madhav Kampo,
where the notification under Section 4 was issued on the same date i.e. 09.06.2005, the market value was determined at the rate of Rs.317 per square meter.

Though it is true that the District Road of village Madhav Kampo directly touches the State Highway, considering the fact that village Dakhneshwar also shares common boundaries with Taluka Bayad, which touches the State Highway, this Court is of the opinion that the award passed in LAR No.2 of 2019 pertaining to village Madhav Kampo would be the proper and comparable instance for determination of the market value.
8 Resultantly, the First Appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned judgment and award is modified to the extent that the market value of the acquired land is determined at the rate of Rs.317 per square meter.
The learned Reference Court shall pay the difference amount to the claimant, after deducting the amount already paid, along with all statutory benefits, within a period of eight weeks from today.
(M. K. THAKKER,J) M.M.MIRZA Patelvasantkumar Revabhai vs State Of Gujarat on 3 March, 2026
